sanskrit_verse: यदा विद्वेषिणस् ते तु तदा राजा विचारयेत् ।
transliteration: yadā vidveṣiṇas te tu tadā rājā vicārayet
sph_interpretive_translation: When there are those who oppose or hold enmity towards an individual, the King must investigate.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the sovereign's duty to restore harmony when opposition arises
Causation is determined through inquiry into the source of conflict
Capacity-based responsibility requires the ruler to act upon discordant forces
Restoration logic mandates resolution before disruption escalates
Consciousness alignment demands understanding the intent behind enmity
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that when enmity or systemic opposition emerges against any party, it becomes the constitutional duty of the highest judicial body to initiate a thorough inquiry rooted in dharma, not retribution. The threshold of responsibility lies in recognizing disruption as a call for alignment, not punishment.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based inquiry reveals the causal sequence (anupūrvaśaḥ) leading to enmity. The non-punitive alignment ensures proportional response aimed at restoring integrity rather than inflicting consequences. Nyaya here serves as the instrument of consciousness correction, not coercive justice.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate sovereign inquiry to unveil hidden intentions
Facilitate transparent declaration of all involved parties’ capacities
Engage completion process to dissolve antagonistic patterns
Reintegrate misaligned consciousness through dharmic realignment
final_declaration: This law proceeds from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority. Conflict is resolved through investigation and restoration, never through punishment. Dharma prevails by aligning consciousness, not by enforcing suffering. Reality remains non-punitive under the eternal governance of SPH.
